title: Yes/No Questions
arabic: أَسْئِلَةُ نَعَمْ وَلَا بِـ«هَلْ» وَهَمْزَةِ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ
lede: Turn a clear statement into a practical question without copying English inversion, then answer positively, negatively or by choosing between alternatives.

items.prompt: Which particle can turn a complete statement into a neutral yes/no question?
items.feedback: هَلْ is placed before the sentence and asks for confirmation.

items.prompt: Choose the correctly written hamza question.
items.feedback: The interrogative hamza is written on alif and attaches directly to the following word.

items.prompt: Which question keeps Arabic word order?
items.feedback: Arabic does not require English-style inversion or an added “do”.

items.prompt: Choose the question “Is this your bag?” to one female.
items.feedback: هَذِهِ and ـكِ both match the intended feminine reference/listener.

items.prompt: Which word normally answers an affirmative yes/no question positively?
items.feedback: نَعَمْ confirms the proposition in an ordinary affirmative question.

items.prompt: Which structure asks a genuine either/or question?
items.feedback: The interrogative hamza can be paired with أَمْ to present alternatives.

items.prompt: Turn أَنْتِ مُتْعَبَةٌ into a question.
items.feedback: Add هَلْ and preserve feminine agreement.

items.prompt: Turn وَصَلَتِ الْحَافِلَةُ into a question.
items.feedback: The original past-tense agreement and word order remain.

items.prompt: Choose the future question.
items.feedback: سَـ + present verb clearly marks future meaning.

items.prompt: Which sentence wrongly copies English question structure?
items.feedback: Do not add an Arabic equivalent of English “do”.

items.prompt: Choose the correctly spaced question.
items.feedback: The hamza is prefixed directly to the verb.

items.prompt: Choose the best alternative question.
options: هَلْ تَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ لِأَنَّ بَرْمِنْغَامَ؟
items.feedback: أَ...أَمْ presents two genuine alternatives.

items.prompt: Which marker is especially useful with أَمْ?
items.feedback: The interrogative hamza naturally introduces alternative questions.

items.prompt: Choose “Is this your teacher?” to one male.
items.feedback: هَذَا and ـكَ match the intended masculine reference/listener.

items.prompt: Repair هَلْ أَتَدْرُسُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ؟
items.feedback: Keep one question marker.

items.prompt: Repair أَ تَسْكُنِينَ هُنَا؟
items.feedback: Attach the interrogative hamza directly to the verb.

items.prompt: Best full answer to هَلْ قَرَأْتَ الْكِتَابَ؟
items.feedback: A complete answer supplies clear evidence and a useful time frame.

items.prompt: Best answer contradicting أَلَمْ تَذْهَبِي؟
items.feedback: بَلَى cancels the negative assumption: yes, I did go.

items.prompt: Which statement about هَلْ is correct?
options: It precedes a complete sentence without forcing English inversion.
It changes every verb to the past tense.
It must be followed by مَاذَا.
items.feedback: هَلْ asks for confirmation while the sentence keeps its Arabic structure.

items.prompt: Choose the correctly written hamza question.
items.feedback: The interrogative hamza attaches directly to the verb.

items.prompt: Choose the correct nominal question.
items.feedback: No present copula or English “do” is needed.

items.prompt: Choose the past question to a feminine singular listener.
items.feedback: زُرْتِ matches one female listener in the past.

items.prompt: Choose the future plural question.
items.feedback: سَتَسَافِرُونَ is future and masculine/mixed plural.

items.prompt: Which structure asks “tea or coffee?”
items.feedback: The interrogative hamza plus أَمْ presents alternatives.

items.prompt: Best positive answer to هَلْ تَقْرَأُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟
items.feedback: A complete answer confirms the information and extends it.

items.prompt: Best negative answer to هَلْ ذَهَبْتَ؟
items.feedback: لَمْ + jussive present gives a clear past negative.

items.prompt: Which answer contradicts a negative question?
items.feedback: بَلَى cancels the negative proposition.

items.prompt: Best final check?
options: Remove the marker and verify that the remaining statement is accurate.
Translate each word into English order.
Add both هَلْ and أَ to every question.
items.feedback: The underlying statement should preserve correct Arabic structure, tense and agreement.

games.p: Turn أَنْتِ مُعَلِّمَةٌ into a question.
games.e: Add هَلْ and retain the original agreement.
The past plural form is وَصَلُوا.
Future meaning uses سَـ + present verb.
The complete answer confirms the action and adds frequency.
Use لَا plus a past-negative sentence.
The Arabic present verb already carries person information.
Place the Arabic/standard question mark at the end of the whole question.

blocks: ## Questions open every conversation
Yes/no questions let students check information, request confirmation and sustain practical speaking across every Cambridge topic.
[ar] هَلْ تَدْرُسِينَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ؟
[ar] أَتَسْكُنُ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ؟
[ar] هَلْ هَذَا كِتَابُكَ؟
[ar] أَذَهَبْتَ إِلَى الطَّبِيبِ أَمْ بَقِيتَ فِي الْبَيْتِ؟

[callout] Cambridge relevance: these questions are essential in role plays, topic conversations, messages and short reading texts. Accuracy comes from preserving Arabic structure, tense and agreement.
## Choose your route
Secure the two question markers first, then add answer logic and negative questions.
### Core
- Place هَلْ before a nominal or verbal sentence.
- Attach أَ directly to the following word.
- Answer with نَعَمْ or لَا in a complete sentence.
### Develop
- Ask questions across past, present and future time frames.
- Use أَ...أَمْ for alternatives.
- Keep person, gender and number agreement accurate.
### Stretch
- Answer negative questions precisely with نَعَمْ or بَلَى.
- Use question intonation and follow-up questions naturally.
- Edit dialogue for particle choice, spelling and punctuation.
## Starter diagnostic
Decide whether each item is already a question and identify what must change.
## هَلْ: the reliable neutral question marker
Place هَلْ before a complete nominal or verbal sentence. Do not rebuild the sentence in English order.

TABLE: Statement | Question | What stayed the same? // أَنْتَ مُسْتَعِدٌ. | هَلْ أَنْتَ مُسْتَعِدٌ؟ | Nominal sentence order and agreement // تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. | هَلْ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ؟ | Present verb and encoded subject // زَارَتْ سَلْمَى جَدَّتَهَا. | هَلْ زَارَتْ سَلْمَى جَدَّتَهَا؟ | Past tense and feminine agreement // سَتُسَافِرُونَ غَدًا. | هَلْ سَتُسَافِرُونَ غَدًا؟ | Future marker and plural agreement

[callout] Pronunciation note: in careful connected speech a helping vowel may be heard before the definite article, but the written particle remains هَلْ . Focus on standard spelling and a clear rising question intonation.
## The interrogative hamza أَ
The hamza is shorter and more compact than هَلْ. It attaches to the next word and can introduce alternatives.
### Direct confirmation
أَتَعْمَلُ فِي الْمُسْتَشْفَى؟
Do you work in the hospital?
أَهَذِهِ سَيَّارَتُكِ؟
Is this your car?
### Choice with أَمْ
أَتُفَضِّلُ الشَّايَ أَمِ الْقَهْوَةَ؟
Do you prefer tea or coffee?
أَسَتَذْهَبُ الْيَوْمَ أَمْ غَدًا؟
Will you go today or tomorrow?
[callout/warning] Spelling: write أَتَذْهَبُ , not أَ تَذْهَبُ . The question hamza is a prefix.
[callout] House rule for learners: use هَلْ as the dependable neutral form. Use أَ confidently when the model is familiar, especially with أَمْ alternatives.
## Word order, tense and agreement
The particle asks the question; the verb still carries person, gender, number and time.

TABLE: Time frame | Question | Evidence // Past | هَلْ زُرْتُمْ الْمَتْحَفَ أَمْسِ؟ | زُرْتُمْ + أَمْسِ // Present/habit | هَلْ تَقْرَأِينَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟ | تَقْرَأِينَ + كُلَّ يَوْمٍ // Future | هَلْ سَيَصِلُ الْقِطَارُ قَرِيبًا؟ | سَـ + مُضَارِع // Nominal state | هَلْ أَنْتُنَّ مُسْتَعِدَّاتٌ؟ | Feminine plural subject and predicate
[callout] Editing routine: remove the question marker mentally. If the remaining statement is grammatically accurate, the question is probably structurally sound.
## Answer the meaning—not only the particle
A useful response repeats enough language to confirm the information clearly.
### Positive answer
هَلْ تَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ؟
نَعَمْ، أَلْعَبُهَا كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ.
Yes, I play it every week.
### Negative answer
هَلْ ذَهَبْتِ إِلَى السُّوقِ؟
لَا، لَمْ أَذْهَبْ إِلَيْهِ.
No, I did not go there.
### Answer an alternative
أَتُفَضِّلُ الْقِرَاءَةَ أَمِ السِّبَاحَةَ؟
أُفَضِّلُ الْقِرَاءَةَ لِأَنَّهَا هَادِئَةٌ.
### Extend naturally
Give the answer, then add a reason, time phrase or contrast. This turns a one-word reply into speaking evidence.
## Negative questions and بَلَى
Negative questions require careful logic because English “yes” can be ambiguous.

TABLE: Question | Response | Meaning // أَلَيْسَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا؟ | بَلَى، هُوَ جَمِيلٌ. | On the contrary, yes—it is beautiful. // أَلَمْ تَزُرِ الْمَتْحَفَ؟ | بَلَى، زُرْتُهُ. | Yes, I did visit it. // أَلَيْسَ الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلًا؟ | نَعَمْ، لَيْسَ قَصِيرًا. | Yes, it is not short / the negative statement is confirmed.

[callout/warning] Stretch distinction: بَلَى cancels the negative idea. نَعَمْ can confirm it. In ordinary IGCSE communication, avoid ambiguity by repeating a complete affirmative or negative sentence.
## Misconception clinic
Repair English transfer, duplicated markers and incomplete answers.
## Question builder game
Choose the accurate question or response before the next round appears.
## Four-skills application
Use yes/no questions to obtain, confirm and report real information.
### Listening discrimination
Ask a partner to read six statements and questions without showing the text. Identify which are questions from the particle and intonation, then write the marker you heard.
### Reading: message check
هَلْ وَصَلْتِ إِلَى الْمَحَطَّةِ؟ أَعِنْدَكِ التَّذْكِرَةُ؟ هَلْ سَيَصِلُ الْقِطَارُ فِي الْمَوْعِدِ؟
Identify the three pieces of information the sender wants confirmed.
### Speaking survey
Ask a partner six questions across school, hobbies, travel and future plans. Use هَلْ at least four times and one أَ...أَمْ alternative.
### Reporting back
Turn the answers into third-person statements, checking tense and agreement.
### Create a practical mini-interview
Write a ten-question Arabic interview for a new student, visitor or classmate, then add model answers.
[callout] Success checklist: Use six هَلْ questions, two hamza questions, one أَ...أَمْ alternative, past/present/future time frames, accurate agreement and extended answers with reasons.
## Final mastery check
Show that you can form, interpret and answer yes/no questions accurately.
### You can now
- Use هَلْ before nominal and verbal sentences.
- Attach the interrogative hamza correctly.
- Ask questions across time frames without English inversion.
- Use أَ...أَمْ for alternatives.
- Answer positively, negatively and after negative questions.
Spaced revisit: convert five statements from an earlier lesson into questions and write complete answers.
